edition_title: Native futex for TOSLightLock and ICU deadlock fix
intro: Today's commits bring a major evolution to the mORMot 2 core synchronization primitives. TOSLightLock now leverages native futex on Linux and WaitOnAddress on Windows 8+, promising significant contention performance gains. In addition, an ICU library deadlock was fixed and the async networking polling got a boundary check.
tldr: TOSLightLock uses native futex on Linux and WaitOnAddress on Windows 8+.
TIcuLibrary fixes a deadlock during shared converter creation.
TAsyncConnections fixes a potential out-of-range bug in thread polling.
Adaptive spin-wait mechanisms are extracted to the core base unit.
upgrade_advice: Teams pushing heavy multithreaded workloads on Linux or Windows 8+ should benefit from the TOSLightLock upgrade. The ICU deadlock fix is recommended for applications dealing with internationalization.

themes.title: Futex-based TOSLightLock
themes.summary: The TOSLightLock structure was heavily refactored across several commits. On Linux, it now uses a 32-bit futex syscall instead of falling back to thread yielding. On Windows 8 and later, it replaces the Slim Reader/Writer (SRW) locks with the faster WaitOnAddress API. A fallback to TRTLCriticalSection remains for older kernels or Android.

themes.title: Adaptive spinning refactoring
themes.summary: The CPU-specific adaptive spin loop functions were centralized. NextSpin() and a new raw DoPause procedure are now public in mormot.core.base, allowing better code reuse across the framework.

entries.headline: Fixed TOSLightLock fallback on Android and Delphi POSIX
entries.what_changed: Restores the TRTLCriticalSection fallback for TOSLightLock on platforms without native futex or pthread_mutex support, like Android and Delphi POSIX. The previous commits inadvertently broke this fallback.
entries.impact: Applications running on Android or compiled with Delphi for POSIX will compile and run correctly again. No impact on Windows or FPC Linux.

entries.headline: Fixed a deadlock when loading ICU converters
entries.what_changed: Corrects the unlock logic in TIcuLibrary.SharedUcnvGet(). The previous code mistakenly released a converter-specific lock instead of the main library lock after populating the converter cache.
entries.impact: Prevents deadlocks when multiple threads request text converters from the ICU library simultaneously.
entries.action_detail: Pull this commit if your server relies heavily on ICU internationalization functions.

entries.headline: Refactored TIcuLibrary internal locking fields
entries.what_changed: Changes the internal locking fields in TIcuLibrary from PtrUInt to cardinal to match the expected types for TLightLock primitives.
entries.impact: No impact on application code, internal refactoring only.

entries.headline: Fixed late loading of Windows 8 synchronization API
entries.what_changed: Moves the runtime loading of API-MS-Win-Core-Synch-l1-2-0.dll to happen after the OS version has been properly populated into OSVersion32.
entries.impact: Resolves a bug where the new futex API was not initialized correctly on modern Windows versions because the version check failed at initialization time.

entries.headline: TOSLightLock uses WaitOnAddress on Windows 8+
entries.what_changed: Upgrades TOSLightLock on Windows to use the WaitOnAddress and WakeByAddressSingle API (introduced in Windows 8), moving away from Slim Reader/Writer (SRW) locks.
entries.impact: Faster lock acquisition on Windows 8 and newer, especially under high contention, by avoiding SRW lock overhead.

entries.headline: Fixed potential bounds error in asynchronous connections
entries.what_changed: Updates TAsyncConnections.ThreadPollingWakeupLocked to check for <= 0 instead of exactly 0 when inspecting spare events.
entries.impact: Prevents potential out-of-range errors or negative event counters from causing issues in the async polling thread loop.

entries.headline: Updated TOSLightLock usage comments
entries.what_changed: Updates code comments referencing TOSLightLock across several units to reflect the new Windows 8+ and Linux futex behaviors.
entries.impact: No impact on application code, internal refactoring only.

entries.headline: TOSLightLock upgraded to use native futex on Linux
entries.what_changed: Replaces the underlying Linux implementation of TOSLightLock with a direct 32-bit futex syscall instead of a TRTLCriticalSection. It falls back to spin-and-wait on older kernels.
entries.impact: Significantly improves requests-per-second and threading stability on Linux backends. It is now as fast as TLightLock on the uncontended fast path.

entries.headline: Published a raw DoPause procedure
entries.what_changed: Extracts the CPU pause logic (the pause opcode on x86, yield on ARM) into a globally available DoPause procedure in mormot.core.base.
entries.impact: Developers can now explicitly call DoPause in custom spin loops to reduce CPU power consumption and cache traffic.

api_changes.note: A cross-platform procedure that invokes CPU pause or yield instructions.

entries.headline: Moved NextSpin to mormot.core.base
entries.what_changed: Moves the adaptive spin-wait function NextSpin() and its associated SPIN_FACTOR and SPIN_COUNT constants from mormot.core.os into the lower-level mormot.core.base unit.
entries.impact: No direct impact on application code. It allows simpler units without OS dependencies to use the adaptive spin logic.
